Lexi Conquest: French (Canada / France), 3–11 playable tiles

Derived lexical data and frequency-based selections: CC BY-SA 4.0.
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
Full license: CC-BY-SA-4.0.txt in this directory. Game code has its separate license.

Lexical data: English Wiktionary contributors, French entries, extracted by
Wiktextract and distributed by Kaikki. Both varieties share a common French
core. Accepted guesses are filtered by supplied regional-sense labels and
known inflection targets, with reviewed exceptions for incomplete source labels. An explicitly reviewed starter selection
adds regional vocabulary and prioritizes labelled senses. A word preferred as an answer for
one variety is not thereby invalid in the other. Regional filtering is bounded
by incomplete source coverage, not an exhaustive national-dictionary claim. Some Canadian additions are
specifically Québécois; this does not represent all Canadian French usage.
Source: https://kaikki.org/dictionary/French/kaikki.org-dictionary-French.jsonl
Source index and rights: https://kaikki.org/dictionary/
Source entry links: https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/<original-headword>#French
Reuse terms: https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Terms_of_Use#7._Licensing_of_Content

The pinned input is Kaikki's postprocessed per-language snapshot, deprecated
upstream, not the raw multilingual Wiktextract extract. Imported 2026-11-06.
SHA-256: 9053b1845fb3e045fa1fbe3f749122fa43e21b49bfa741cadd50255ae6ca0126
No exact per-entry article revision is supplied. Per-record input hashes and
original spellings are retained in the repository. Credit: Tatu Ylonen,
Wiktextract: Wiktionary as Machine-Readable Structured Data, LREC 2022,
pp. 1317-1325, https://www.lrec-conf.org/proceedings/lrec2022/pdf/2022.lrec-1.140.pdf

Changes: retain lowercase French headwords with 3–11 playable tiles, spelling
frequency Zipf >= 2.5 or a listed lexical review candidate, parts of speech,
selected English glosses, usage labels and form/alternative relationships.
Exclude enrichment categories/disambiguation, audio, media, quotations,
examples, etymology, translations and non-Latin spellings. Preserve accents,
cedilla and ligatures in original source spelling and definition attribution.
The grid explicitly expands Œ to OE and Æ to AE (two tiles each). Comparison
ignores accents, diaeresis and cedilla; Ç matches C. One answer per folded
spelling prevents duplicate equivalent candidates. Canonical reveal metadata
restores ligatures. The wider guess dictionary is separate from the conservative
reviewed answer subset. Source usage labels and editorial exclusions filter
answers, not every displayed sense. At most eight entries and eight senses per
entry are displayed per spelling. Plain guesses may combine accent-equivalent
spellings; exact accented reveals keep their own meaning.

Frequency metadata: wordfreq v3.0.2, Robyn Speer and contributors, revision
372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b, small_fr.msgpack.gz.
https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq/tree/372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b
SHA-256: 8fbbf619ff2e6ff5b3d99d41e69c105daf5795771ce8ef36529f210d571abe6e
Data: CC BY-SA 4.0. Version 3.0.2 software: MIT. Complete pinned README and
MIT notice are supplied in this directory. Preserve all README source credits,
including OpenSubtitles and freely available SUBTLEX, Marc Brysbaert and
coauthors. No corpus sentences are distributed. Retained spelling estimates
are historical, not current sense-specific or Canada/France measurements.
For case/ligature merged spellings, use the maximum estimate, not a sum.

No native-human review or exhaustive regional dictionary coverage is claimed.
Source extraction, labels and model editorial review can contain errors.
Dictionary glosses are not full lessons or usage guarantees. Authored example
sentences are not included. Meaning availability never determines whether a
word is accepted as a guess. No words are automatically sent to an external
service by the game.

Sources, checksums, policy and offline reproduction are documented in
src/data/french/source.json and docs/french-varieties.md in the source repository:
https://github.com/intrepion/kata-inspired-by-wordle-codex-dot
Preserve attribution, modification notices and CC BY-SA 4.0 ShareAlike terms
when redistributing adapted data. These notices add no extra restrictions.
